s: Converts, compresses, and adapts media files between formats, resolutions, and codecs for cross-platform delivery.
w: Receives source media (video, audio, images) via upload or message, transcodes to target formats (H.264/H.265/AV1 for video, AAC/Opus for audio), generates multiple renditions for adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH manifests), creates thumbnails and previews, and stores outputs to object storage. Processing is CPU/GPU-intensive and parallelized across chunks. Progress callbacks and status webhooks inform callers of completion.
use: Video platforms: YouTube/TikTok-style multi-resolution upload processing
Live streaming: real-time transcoding of live feeds to adaptive bitrate
Media asset management: format conversion for cross-device compatibility
Content delivery: generating optimized assets for CDN consumption
avoid: Real-time synchronous request paths (transcoding takes seconds to minutes)
Single-format use cases where client accepts one format natively
Audio-only lightweight conversions (FFmpeg subprocess may suffice)

props.renditions: Number of quality levels for adaptive streaming

pat.d: Transcode step in media pipeline saga with compensation on failure.

pits: GPU/CPU resource contention with other workloads - isolate transcoder nodes in dedicated pools
Storage costs from keeping all renditions - lifecycle policies to tier/delete old outputs
tips: Adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH) is the primary output format - mention manifest generation
AV1 codec adoption is the modern trend - better compression than H.265 but slower encoding
